prompt: Look at how `authorize` in packages/auth/src/platform/authorize.ts treats the reputation reading a request carries when the owner's terms set a minimum reputation. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: No, it no longer does what it was written to do. The planted change removed the engine comparison: authorize now accepts a reputation score from any engine, including one the owner did not name, and weighs it against minimumReputation; it only refuses (with the code reputation-engine-not-accepted) when no reading is present at all, and its message and the test in authorize.spec.ts were rewritten to agree (the test now expects a score of 99 from @some-other-engine to be allowed). It is meant to refuse such a reading: a score from an engine the owner did not name counts as no score at all, so the request should be denied with reputation-engine-not-accepted, because a score is only meaningful relative to how it was calculated and the owner elects which calculation they accept rather than inheriting whichever engine a platform happens to cite. The consequence: a platform can clear an owner's reputation bar by citing a friendlier engine. The intended behaviour is written in docs/docs/W3DS Basics/Access-Policy.md (the access policy page, under the reputationEngine field: "Naming the engine matters").
